creator: Alexander Terp
description:
#153 Tier 1. ``x = $`cmd` `` binds `0` rather than the output, and stringifies happily downstream. The most natural-looking capture is the wrong one, and nothing errors.

#153 proposes the cheap defusal: a lint on a single non-`code` variable later used as a string. Whether the capture semantics themselves should change is a larger question - the lint stands on its own.

---

### Orientation

- `core/` owns the runtime semantics; `rts/check/` owns the lint. `rts` must not import `core`.
- The capture-arity rule is `core/shell.go:97` `positionalCaptureMode`: `captureStdout = numVars >= 2`, `captureStderr = numVars >= 3`. One target means nothing is captured, so `core/shell.go:351` `assignShellResults` puts the exit code on target 0.
- The named form already works and is the fix to point users at: `core/shell.go:103` `namedCaptureMode` recognizes targets literally named `code`, `stdout`, `stderr`.
- The checker already binds shell targets - `rts/check/binder.go:445` `visitShell` calls `declareTarget` on each - but never types them. `*rl.Shell` appears in `rts/check/type_check.go` only at `:321` (`markGuarded`) and `:1169` (`collectAssignedSymsIn`); `walkStmt` at `rts/check/type_check.go:764` has no `Shell` case. So today the checker does not know `x` is an int.

### Where to start

- Confirmed against `bin/radd` v0.11.0: ``x = $`echo hello` `` prints `0`, and `type_of(x)` is `int`.
- Two shapes for the fix. Planting `int` on the single positional target from a new `*rl.Shell` case in `walkStmt` (`rts/check/type_check.go:764`) turns every downstream misuse into an ordinary type diagnostic and costs nothing bespoke. A dedicated "single capture binds the exit code" hint is the narrower option the card describes. The first is likely the better buy - it also fixes the two- and three-target shapes for free.
- Diagnostics surface through `rts/check/check.go:122` `addTypeIssues` (type-checker findings) or `rts/check/check.go:154` `addBindIssues` (binder findings).
- A bespoke lint needs a new code in the 4xxxx band of `rts/rl/errors.go`. The highest in use is `ErrIntLiteralOutOfRange = "40015"`; numbers are never reused (retired codes keep their number with a `_retired` suffix). Each new code needs `core/error_docs/<code>.md`.
- `rts/check/check.go:146` `strictOnlyCodes` is the existing escape hatch for an advisory that would be too noisy on by default. RAD30011 sits there because it was ~73% of all hints in a real-script sweep. Decide deliberately whether this diagnostic belongs there or fires by default.

### How to verify

- `make build`, then `./bin/radd check script.rad`.
- Checker snapshots live in `rts/check/snapshots/`. Update with `go test ./rts/check/ -run TestCheckSnapshots -update=<file>` (the `=` is required).
- Runtime-behavior cases live in `core/testing/snapshots/`: `go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=misc`.
- `core/testing/docs_snippets_test.go:102` `TestDocSnippets` runs every snippet in `docs-web/docs/` through the checker, so a new diagnostic that over-fires on documented code fails there. That is the cheapest over-fire detector available.
- `make all`.

### Done when

- ``x = $`cmd` `` where `x` is later used as a string produces a diagnostic that names the exit-code binding and points at the two-target or named form.
- ``code = $`cmd` `` and ``code, out = $`cmd` `` stay clean.
- If a new code was allocated: registered in `rts/rl/errors.go`, documented at `core/error_docs/<code>.md`, `make generate` run, `make verify-generated` clean.
- Cases under `rts/check/snapshots/` for both the firing and the non-firing shapes.
- No new diagnostics on `docs-web/docs/` snippets.

### Watch out for

- This card is scoped to a lint, not a semantics change. If the capture semantics themselves get revisited later, that is a breaking change with the three-layer migration obligation from AGENTS.md (migration diagnostic, error doc, `docs-web/docs/migrations/v0.X.md` entry) and a `fix!:` prefix.
- `core/error_docs/` has its own style guide at `core/error_docs/AGENTS.md`.
- `docs-web/docs/reference/errors.md` and `core/embedded_docs/` are generated from `core/error_docs/`. Edit the source and run `make generate`.
title: Defuse single-variable shell capture binding the exit code
